chapter_name: Introducing Ayurveda The Science of Health and Disease
learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the holistic principles of Ayurveda, the ancient Indian science of life, balance, and healing, which treats the root cause rather than just the symptoms.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Ayurveda (Ayus = Life, Veda = Knowledge) is the ancient Indian system of medicine. It focuses on holistic health—balancing the body, mind, and spirit—rather than just treating diseases.
Ayurveda believes everything in the universe, including our bodies, is made of 5 elements: Space (Akasha), Air (Vayu), Fire (Tejas), Water (Jala), and Earth (Prithvi).

The 5 elements combine to form 3 Doshas (biological energies) that control the body: Vata (Air+Space, controls movement), Pitta (Fire+Water, controls digestion/metabolism), and Kapha (Earth+Water, controls structure/lubrication). Disease happens when these are unbalanced.

These are the two foundational texts of Ayurveda. The 'Charaka Samhita' focuses on internal medicine (diagnostics and herbs), while the 'Sushruta Samhita' focuses on advanced surgery, including rhinoplasty (plastic surgery).

Ayurveda emphasizes prevention through lifestyle. 'Dinacharya' means following a healthy daily routine (like waking early, yoga, proper diet), and 'Ritucharya' means adjusting your diet and habits according to the changing seasons.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ Discover Your Dosha
fun_activity.instructions: Are you mostly cold, active, and creative (Vata)? Warm, focused, and prone to anger (Pitta)? Or calm, solid, and deep sleeping (Kapha)? Search for a 'Dosha Quiz' online to discover your unique 'Prakriti' (body constitution)!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the three Doshas (Vata, Pitta, Kapha) and link them to their respective elements.
📌 Distinguish between the 'Charaka Samhita' (Internal Medicine) and 'Sushruta Samhita' (Surgery).
📌 Remember that Ayurveda treats the *patient* based on their unique 'Prakriti', not just the *disease*.
quick_recap: ⭐ Health in Ayurveda is a perfect balance of Doshas, Dhatus, and a happy mind.
⭐ Sushruta is celebrated globally as the 'Father of Surgery'.
⭐ Diet (Ahara) is considered the most important medicine in Ayurveda.
